nodes.question: What is a specific wild relative mentioned that could contribute to improving drought tolerance in wheat?
nodes.answer: Aegilops tauschii is mentioned as a wild relative that could contribute to improving drought tolerance.
nodes.paragraph: Adaptive variation uncovered by GWES in wild relatives has the potential to improve climate resilience of crop varieties. nodes.question: At what plant density was the sorghum sown?
nodes.answer: The sorghum was sown at a plant density of 120,000 plants ha⁻¹.
nodes.paragraph: Cow dung was applied at the rate of 5130 kg ha 1 per year as manure fertilizer. The previous sea- son S crop straw was used for the straw application. Detailed nitrogen, phosphorous, and potassium nutrient inputs for each treatment are provided in Table S1. Application of manure and straw were performed follow - ing the crop harvest in the Autumn. Diammonium phos- phate and potassium sulphate, along with 50% of the N fertilizer (the N shortage was replenished by urea), were applied before sowing in the Spring. The remaining N fer - tilizer as urea was applied at the bolting stage. A popular sorghum cultivar, Jinza 31, was seeded with a plant den- sity of 120,0 plant ha 1 in April 2020, and harvested in September 2020. The growing season experienced no obvi- ous issues with pests, diseases, or weed infestations. Soils attached to the surface of five sorghum plant roots were col - lected at the jointing, heading, filling and maturity stages in 2020 as rhizosphere soils. The rhizosphere soil samples were immediately taken to the laboratory and sieved soils to < 2 mm, and stored at 80 C for molecular analyses.

nodes.question: What types of grains do villagers grow that are drought tolerant?
nodes.answer: Villagers grow sorghum (Sorghum bicolor), millet (Pennisetum glaucum), and rapoko (Eleusine coracana) which are drought tolerant.
nodes.paragraph: However, villagers grow small grains which are droughttolerant such as sorghum ( Sorghum bicolor ), millet ( Pen- nisetum glaucum ), and rapoko ( Eleusine coracana ). They also grow maize at a smaller scale. Small scale livestock production rearing domestic animals like cattle, pigs, goats and drought power animals like donkeys is also practiced. There is commercial agriculture to the south and east of SVC. Some local people get part time and/ full time jobs on these estates. Data Collection Methods Primary data collection Questionnaire surveys Semi-structured questionnaire sur- veys were done with two groups of respondents, illegal hunters and eld rangers. Data were collected using an interview administered questionnaire in the local language(Shona). Throughout the study, anonymity of the respon- dents was maintained, and it was made clear that the information collected was solely for research purposes.Respondents were informed that the surveys would be anonymous and were part of a university study assessing wildlife and rural livelihoods. The study adhered to ethicalstandards to ensure that the rights and welfare of the par- ticipants were protected. To gain a comprehensive under- standing of the nature and extent of poaching in SVC, thequestionnaire had both open-ended and closed-ended questions.

nodes.question: What is sorghum recognized for in terms of its agricultural characteristics?
nodes.answer: Sorghum is known for its exceptional tolerance of drought and barren conditions.
nodes.paragraph: Additionally, bacterial communities were reported to have a higher microbial temporal stability compared to fungal communities (Lange et al. 2023), whereas Chen et al. (2019) demonstrated a stronger influence of plant growth stages on bacterial communities than on fungal communities. Despite these progresses, our knowledge of the relative temporal sta- bility of bacteria and fungi remains unclear, especially under different chemical and organic fertilizer regimes. Sorghum, known for its exceptional tolerance of drought and barren (Gao et al. 2020), is the 5th most widely culti- vated cereal crop worldwide and a vital resource for ensuring food security. The rhizosphere is an important compartment for microbiomes that can predict crop yield and protein (Liu et al. 2023) and is more significantly affected by organic and inorganic fertilization treatments relative to other crop com- partments (Sun et al. 2021). In this study, we characterized sorghum rhizosphere community structure of bacteria and fungi, based on a long-term field experiment initiated in 2011. This study aimed to (i) whether organic fertilizer enhanced temporal variations in rhizosphere bacterial and fungal com- munities; and (ii) assess the stability of both bacterial and fun- gal communities across different sorghum growth stages.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water conservation practices|Drought-tolerant crop cultivation_qna_004
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How does drought stress affect maize according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Drought stress adversely affects water uptake, can stunt growth, and reduces the overall productivity of maize.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Maize is the third most important grain crop worldwide after wheat and rice; it is a vital global crop, serving as a key source of food, animal feed, and industrial products, making it essential for food security and economic stability in many countries. Drought stress adversely affects water uptake and can stunt growth, reducing the overall produc tivity of maize. So, this study was carried out to investigate the cytogenetic effects of gamma radiation and drought stress on maize SC131 genotype, focusing on chromosomal aberrations in seedling root meristems induced by vary ing doses of gamma irradiation (50, 100, 150, 200, and 250 Gray) and drought stress imposed by 10% polyethyl ene glycol (PEG). The present study also aims to evaluate the impact of these treatments on growth parameters under a controlled pot experiment. Additionally, molecular polymorphism induced by both gamma irradiation and drought stress was analyzed using Real Time quantitative PCR techniques for DREB2, ERF, and EF transcrip tion factors. Also, under a field condition experiment, maize plants were subjected to the same gamma irradiation doses and drought stress by reducing the number of irrigations, with subsequent evaluations of yield attributes to assess the overall impact of treatments on plant performance.

nodes.question: What characteristic of maize allows it to efficiently use moisture and sunlight?
nodes.answer: Maize is a C4 species, which allows it to efficiently use moisture and sunlight to produce high yield and total dry matter.
nodes.paragraph: The study also investigates the sodium dodecyl sulfate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS PAGE) banding patterns of proteins in grains yielded under the influ ence of gamma radiation and drought treatments. Findings of the current investigation indicate that the low dose of gamma radiation (50 Gray) not only induces cytogenetic changes but also enhances drought tolerance and improves yield characteristics, suggesting that targeted gamma irradiation could serve as a viable strategy to bol ster maize resilience in challenging environmental conditions. Keywords Maize, Gamma radiation, Drought, Growth and yield traits, Chromosomal aberrations, RT PCR, SDS PAGE Introduction Maize (Zea mays L.) is a diploid (2n = 2x = 20), annual, monoecious cereal of the family Poaceae (Gramineae). Maize is the third most important grain crop worldwide after wheat and rice [1]. It is widely farmed over the world in a variety of agro-ecological conditions. Maize, a C4 species, uses moisture and sunlight efficiently to produce high yield and total dry matter [2]. Global maize produc - tion is becoming increasingly important as a source of food, forage, oil, and biofuel for the world S growing pop - ulation.

nodes.question: What treatments were the maize grains exposed to in the study?
nodes.answer: The maize grains were exposed to five doses of gamma irradiation and simulated drought treatment using PEG-6000.
nodes.paragraph: BMC Plant Biology (2025) 25:141 attributes of field-grown plants, (5) Study the SDS-PAGE banding pattern of yielded grains protein under the effect of gamma irradiation and drought treatments. Materials and methods Plant material and gamma irradiation Egyptian single cross of maize SC131 (Pedigree: Sakha9 X Sakha5) was used in this study. Grains of this geno - type was obtained from the Maize Research Depart - ment, Field Crops Research Institute of the Agricultural Research Center (ARC) in Giza, Egypt. This genotype was selected from the germplasm based on its agronomic importance as well as its disease-resistant and drought- tolerant properties. Grains were exposed to five doses of gamma irradiation using the Indian Gamma Cell Unit (IGCU) at the Atomic Energy Commission (AEC), Nasr City, Cairo, Egypt, using Co60 as a source of irradiation. The applied doses were 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250 Gray (Dose Rate = 0.960 KGy/h). Grains of control samples were not exposed to gamma irradiation. Cytological procedures For the cytological analyses, two groups were used, first group comprised maize grains that were treated with gamma irradiation doses only and the second group that was treated with the same doses of radiation accompa - nied by the exposure to simulated drought using PEG- 6000 (10%).

nodes.question: Why is the inclusion of pulse crops particularly encouraged in semi-arid cropping systems?
nodes.answer: It is encouraged due to the limited water availability presenting significant challenges to sustainability in those systems.
nodes.paragraph: 2018). The inclu- sion of pulses into simplified rotations is a widely adopted diversification strategy (Hufnagel et al. 2020), as legumes can provide an array of ecological benefits (Ditzler et al. 2021). Some examples are improved N use efficiency (St. Luce et al. 2015), N credit from biological fixation (Bell et al. 2017; Taveira et al. 2020), increased water conserva- tion (Gan et al. 2017; Seymour et al. 2012), reduced N2O emissions (Lemke et al. 2007; Liu et al. 2024), improved soil health (Lal 2017), and enhanced biodiversity (Zander et al. 2016). These valuable ecosystem services encourage farmers to include pulse crops into cereal and oilseed rotations, par - ticularly in semi-arid cropping systems, where limited water availability presents significant challenges to sustainability. Canada leads global lentil and pea production, yielding 2.9 million tonnes of lentils and 4.6 million tonnes of peas in 2021, which accounts for 45% and 31% of world produc - tion (FAO 2024).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water conservation practices|Drought-tolerant crop cultivation_qna_011
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the most limited yield factor in the semi-arid Canadian prairies?
nodes.answer: Water is the most limited yield factor in the semi-arid Canadian prairies.
nodes.paragraph: The Canadian prairies contribute to 98% of the Canadian pea and lentil production (Saskatchewan Pulse Growers 2024). In addition, incorporating pulse crops in wheat-based rotations in the semi-arid Canadian prairies led to economic benefits for producers (Khakbazan et al. 2022). In the semi-arid Canadian prairies, where water is the most limited yield factor, simplified cropping systems negatively impact both non-legume and pulse crop produc- tion, as well as the ecological benefits associated with pulse crops. Therefore, a comprehensive evaluation using multiple indicators collectively is needed on ecosystem services in response to diversification of crop rotations with pulse crops, particularly at the cropping system level in the intermediate term (e.g., 5 10 years). Synergies and trade-offs among ecosystem services are widely recognized and reported in cropping systems (Power 2010 ; Rodr guez et al. 2006 ). However, most studies have often focused on individual ecosystem services, although sustainable cropping systems require a holistic improve- ment in ecosystem services, including crop productivity, resource use efficiency, economic returns, soil health, and environmental health.

nodes.question: Where is the study site located, and what factor significantly limits crop production there?
nodes.answer: The study site is located in the semi-arid region of southern Alberta and Saskatchewan, where water scarcity significantly limits crop production.
nodes.paragraph: Both farmers and researchers are seeking sustainable cropping systems that not only improve productivity and economic returns but also enhance soil health and reduce environmental impacts (Anderson 2011). Balancing productivity, profitability, and environmental sustainability remains a significant challenge (Davis et al. 2012). Therefore, it becomes critical to collectively assess agronomic, economic, and environmental responses to man- agement practices to gain a deeper understanding of eco- system services that underpin sustainable cropping systems (Darnhofer et al. 2010). However, there remains a knowledge gap regarding the overall system performance of diversified rotations using multiple indicators collectively, particularly at the cropping system level. In this study, we evaluated ecosystem services as indi- cated by multiple indicators, including crop productivity, resource use efficiency, soil carbon, economic returns, and environmental impacts, in rotations with different levels of diversification involving pulse crops. In the Canadian prai- ries, wheat and canola dominate crop production; however, simplified wheat-based cropping systems have negatively affected sustainability and resilience (Martens et al. 2015). The study site is located in the semi-arid region of southern Alberta and Saskatchewan, where water scarcity signifi- cantly limits crop production and no till is one of the most common practices for soil and water conservation.
